The **boiling point of water at sea level** is **100 °C (212 °F)** [^3][^6].

While 100 °C is the standard value used for general purposes, the precise scientific measurement under standard atmospheric pressure is approximately **99.97 °C (211.95 °F)** [^1].

Key factors regarding the boiling point of water include:
- **Atmospheric Pressure:** Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of the liquid equals the surrounding atmospheric pressure [^3].
- **Altitude Effects:** As altitude increases, atmospheric pressure decreases, causing water to boil at lower temperatures [^4][^5].
- **Below Sea Level:** Conversely, at locations below sea level where atmospheric pressure is higher, water boils at temperatures slightly above 100 °C (212 °F) [^2].
